newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Arbed slides into first-half loss.
newsitem.headline: Arbed slides into first-half loss.

text.p: Luxembourg-based steel maker Arbed SA said on Tuesday it booked a group loss of 249 million Belgian francs ($7.9 million), reversing a 2.41 billion Luxembourg franc group net profit in the first half of 1995.
But the group said it expected a progressive pick up in its markets and earnings in the coming quarters.

"The end of the phase of de-stocking at our main clients and the accompanying pick-up in demand seems to confirm that the set-back in the steel environment appears to have reached its lowest level in third quarter 1996," Arbed said in a statement.
It added that in these conditions Arbed was counting on a "progressive pick up in its principle markets and in its results in the approaching quarters".
Chairman Joseph Kinsch told a news conference to announce the results, that "the second half 1996 will be good, even if I remain cautious".
He added that 1996 as a whole would "not be a brilliant year" though, with the real effect of the pick-up showing through in 1997.
Kinsch said the expected growth in steel consumption in the European Union in 1997 was 4.9 percent versus a 7.1 percent fall for the first three quarters of 1996.
The group's first-half consolidated turnover fell to 117.35 billion francs, from 135.60 billion. ($1=31.39 Belgian Franc)
